items.fact: The letter concerns a change in the reader's enrollment during the term beginning September 1, 1996, which may have caused an overpayment.
items.quote: This letter is about the change in your enrollment during the period that began on September 1, 1996. Because of this change, we may have paid you more than you were due.
items.where: We are writing to you about a change in your school schedule. Your term started on September 1, 1996. Because of this change, we may have paid you too much money.

items.fact: The term for which the enrollment change applies began on September 1, 1996.
items.quote: the period that began on September 1, 1996
items.where: Your term started on September 1, 1996.

items.fact: The reader reduced credit hours on this date.
items.quote: You reduced your credit hours from 12 hours to 6 hours on November 5, 1996.
items.where: On November 5, 1996, you went from 12 credit hours to 6 credit hours.

items.fact: Credit hours were reduced from 12 to 6.
items.quote: You reduced your credit hours from 12 hours to 6 hours on November 5, 1996.
items.where: you went from 12 credit hours to 6 credit hours

items.fact: Payments were reduced to this monthly amount.
items.quote: We reduced your payments on December 1, 1996 to $202.00 per month.
items.where: we lowered your payment to $202.00 a month

items.fact: The payment reduction took effect on this date.
items.quote: We reduced your payments on December 1, 1996 to $202.00 per month.
items.where: On December 1, 1996, we lowered your payment to $202.00 a month.

items.fact: The reader will receive another letter about the payment change, which will show whether there is a debt.
items.answer: Another letter will follow showing if there is a debt
items.quote: You will receive another letter about this change. The letter will show if you have a debt.
items.where: We will send you another letter about this. That letter will tell you if you owe us money.

items.fact: The reader must send a statement explaining why they reduced their credit hours.
items.answer: Send a statement explaining the reduction
items.quote: Please send us a statement explaining why you reduced the number of your credit hours.
items.where: Please write to us and tell us why you lowered your credit hours.

items.fact: The reader should send evidence supporting the statement.
items.quote: In most cases, we require evidence to support your statement.
items.where: We usually need proof, too.

items.fact: If the reader has no supporting evidence, they should explain why.
items.answer: Explain why there is no evidence
items.quote: If you do not have supporting evidence, please tell us why.
items.where: If you don't have proof, tell us why you don't have it.

items.fact: The statement and evidence are due within 30 days.
items.quote: Send us your statement with any supporting evidence within 30 days.
items.where: Please send us your statement and any proof within 30 days.

items.fact: If the statement is accepted, payments will not be reduced from the term's beginning date.
items.answer: No retroactive reduction to the start of term
items.quote: If we accept your statement, we will not reduce your payments from the beginning date of the term.
items.where: We will not lower your payments back to the start of the term.

items.fact: If the statement is accepted, any debt already created must still be repaid but will not be increased.
items.answer: Existing debt must be repaid, not increased
items.quote: If a debt has already been created it must be repaid, but the debt will not be increased.
items.where: If you already owe us money, you will still have to pay it back. But you will not owe more than that.

items.fact: If the statement and evidence are not accepted, payments will be reduced as of September 1, 1996, creating a debt to repay.
items.quote: If we do not accept your statement with supporting evidence we will reduce your payments on September 1, 1996, the beginning date of the term. This will create a debt which you must repay.
items.where: We will lower your payments starting September 1, 1996. That is the day your term began. This means you will owe us money. You will have to pay it back.
